turns.doctor_question: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because... well, I'm having these thoughts that I just can't get rid of. 

I drive a cab, and even when I know I did my safety check on the car, this thought just keeps hitting me that I missed something. I keep thinking somebody could get hurt, or my boss is gonna say I lied about checking it. And I just... I can't make it shut up. It's constantly there while I'm driving, or even when I'm just trying to study. It's really getting to me.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient reports recurrent, persistent, and intrusive thoughts of pathological doubt regarding vehicle safety checks that they cannot dismiss or suppress.

turns.doctor_question: When these thoughts come up, do you feel driven to check the car again or do something else repeatedly to reduce your anxiety?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. Before I can even take a ride, I just keep going around the car. I check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, my paperwork... I just check them over and over. 

Sometimes I even take pictures of everything to try and prove to myself I did it. And if... if doing the check just doesn't feel right, I have to restart the whole thing from the very beginning. I end up doing it even when passengers are standing right there waiting for me and I'm already late. I just have to do it before I can drive.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes repetitive checking behaviors (tires, doors, meter, taking photos) and repeating rituals from the beginning when it doesn't feel right, confirming compulsions.

turns.doctor_question: Do you recognize that these checking thoughts and urges may be excessive or unreasonable?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. I mean... I know it's way too much. It doesn't make sense to keep looking at the same tires or doors over and over, especially when people are just standing there watching me. 

I know I just checked it a minute ago and it was fine. I know it's unreasonable. But... knowing that doesn't really help. The feeling doesn't go away just because I know it's crazy. I still have to do it anyway.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive checking behaviors (checking tires and doors repeatedly despite knowing it was just checked and is unreasonable).
